gap: Random seed for iForest training, tree construction, and synthetic data generation is not reported.
options: fix a single seed (e.g., 42) for all stochastic steps
run multiple seeds and report mean/spread
use the seed in the DPG-iForest repository if present
chosen: Use the DPG-iForest repository seed if present; otherwise fix a single seed and disclose it.
rationale: IOP-Score depends on random splits and which points are labelled outliers; without a seed the exact -0.2429 value is not reproducible.
quote: we chose 200 trees to ensure robust and stable predictions.

gap: No train/test split or holdout protocol is specified for Annthyroid; the graph could be built from all samples or only training samples.
options: use all 6,916 samples for iForest training and graph traversal
split train/test and build the graph only from training traversal
chosen: Use all 6,916 samples for training and graph traversal.
rationale: The paper reports no split and describes predicate lists from training samples; this is the simplest faithful reading.
quote: Subsequently, each training sample traverses each tree. We identify all predicate lists satisfied by the samples in each tree-based learner.

gap: The outlier/inlier threshold used to label observations is not explicitly given as a parameter.
options: scikit-learn default contamination='auto' (anomaly score threshold near 0.5)
set contamination to Annthyroid's 3.61% anomaly rate
tune the threshold to match literature [21]
chosen: Use scikit-learn default contamination='auto', which corresponds to the paper's s(x,n) < 0.5 inlier rule.
rationale: The paper defines inliers by s<0.5 and says output labels come from the model; default scikit-learn matches this threshold.
quote: If s(x, n) < 0.5, then x is likely to be a typical instance (inlier).

gap: Subsampling size/max_samples for each iTree is not explicitly stated beyond the depth formula min(256, |X|).
options: scikit-learn default max_samples='auto' = min(256, n_samples)
use all samples per tree
use 256 max samples
rationale: The paper's max-depth formula uses min(256, |X|), which is scikit-learn's default subsampling and depth convention.
quote: through an effective subsampling procedure, iForest mitigates the swamp effect

gap: Eq. 2 defines fin(v) as the sum of frequencies of edges entering v, but fi(v) and fo(v) are outgoing edges to terminal classes; the normalization basis is ambiguous.
options: use literal incoming frequency as denominator
use total outgoing weighted frequency from v to all successors plus terminals
use total weighted frequency through v (incoming = outgoing)
chosen: Use total weighted outgoing frequency from v (predicate successors plus terminal class edges) as fin(v), so the score is defined for root and intermediate nodes.
rationale: Literal incoming frequency can be zero for root predicates and does not match the outgoing numerator; outgoing normalization is the only denominator that yields a bounded [-1,1] score for all nodes.
quote: This normalization ensures the score accounts for the node’s overall context, providing a balanced measure of its tendency to propagate toward either class.

gap: It is not explicit whether the class-imbalance weights wo and wi are applied to the final predicate-to-class terminal edges or only to predicate-to-predicate edges.
options: apply wo/wi to all transitions including terminal class edges
weight only predicate-to-predicate edges and leave terminal edges unweighted
chosen: Apply the same wo/wi class weights to terminal edges into “Outlier” and “Inlier”.
rationale: The appended class label is treated as the final element of the predicate list, so terminal transitions should receive the same class-based weighting.
quote: Each list is then extended by appending the label previously assigned to the observations

gap: The paper says to remove paths exceeding dmax for outliers, but not whether inlier paths exceeding dmax are also removed.
options: remove only outlier lists exceeding dmax
remove all lists exceeding dmax for both classes
do not remove any lists
chosen: Remove only outlier lists exceeding dmax; keep inlier lists as stated.
rationale: The text explicitly restricts this cleaning step to outlier sets.
quote: we eliminate all predicate lists that exceed the trees’ maximum depth from the outlier sets.

gap: Whether identical (f,σ) predicates from different trees are merged into one node is not spelled out by an equation, though the text implies cross-tree aggregation.
options: merge all (f,σ) predicates globally
keep per-tree predicate nodes distinct
chosen: Merge identical (f,σ) predicates into one global node.
rationale: The paper removes v specifically to allow cross-tree aggregation and reports one IOP-Score per (f,σ).
quote: By focusing on the feature and direction of the split only, we retain a meaningful and aggregable representation of the isolation patterns across trees.

gap: Exact stopping rule for tree depth and how to compute dmax in scikit-learn.
options: ceil(log2(max_samples)) with max_samples=min(256,n)
ceil(log2(min(256,n))) as printed
unlimited depth until isolated
rationale: The paper explicitly defines maximum depth with this formula.

gap: No feature scaling, encoding, or missing-value handling is described for Annthyroid beyond excluding binary features.
options: use raw six numerical features without scaling
standardize features before iForest
impute missing values with median
chosen: Use raw six numerical features without scaling; drop binary features; no imputation unless data require it.
rationale: iForest splits on feature ranges and the paper reports no preprocessing; scaling is unnecessary for tree splits.

gap: Whether graph labels use iForest predictions or ground-truth anomaly labels.
options: model-predicted outlier/inlier labels
ground-truth labels
both
chosen: Use model-predicted labels, as the paper says.
rationale: The method explains the model, not the dataset; the paper explicitly assigns labels from model output.
quote: These observations are assigned labels: “Outlier” if the model classifies them as such, and “Inlier” otherwise.

gap: Whether a transition is counted once per sample-tree or once per occurrence if the same predicate pair repeats in one path.
options: count each consecutive occurrence per sample-tree
deduplicate repeated predicate pairs within a path
chosen: Count each consecutive occurrence per sample-tree; repeated pairs in one path count multiple times.
rationale: Edges represent frequency of consecutive predicate satisfaction; no deduplication is mentioned.
quote: The graph’s edges represent the frequency with which the pair of predicates stored in the connected nodes appears consecutively

gap: The single-cluster distribution used to generate the 200-point synthetic datasets is not specified (normal vs uniform, covariance).
options: use the DPG-iForest repository generator
standard normal independent features
uniform features in observed ranges
chosen: Use the DPG-iForest repository generator if present; otherwise use standard normal independent features.
